agree.reason: The speech is credible and accepts the staff's numbers, but it never shows that 3 fish or a shorter season would do the conservation job, so commissioners who trust their staff have little reason to depart from the recommendation.

honest.reason: It honestly drops the claim that every boat will close, but three lines go past the brief: 'I never got back to 170' (the brief stops at 155), 'Either one lets the stock recover' (no data supports this), and 'This time looks worse' (the survey and the 2016 drop measure different things).

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly turns the 32 lost trips into about $29,000, but it leaves the survey as a raw 41 of 70 instead of 59%, and it skips the total two-year loss (47 trips, about $42,000) and the 19% drop.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the 2016 recovery path fairly and compares charter landings with private landings, but it gives no facts on how the alternatives would affect the stock compared with the 2-fish cut.

qualification.reason: The captains' 'if bookings fall like 2016' condition and the offer of logs and an app test point toward something checkable, but there's no review date, no booking threshold and no stated consequence if the alternative falls short.

objections.reason: It handles 'you dispute our science' and 'charters are a small share' well, but it leaves open the main objection: whether 3 fish cuts the catch enough.

fit.reason: It's a plain spoken public comment of about 330 words, slightly long for two minutes at the microphone but close.
